preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership)
rewardsPool address must be set (via setRewardsPool)
pair address must be set (via setPair)

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the rebase() function with a large multiple value (e.g., type(uint256).max / currentRebaseMultiple). This will cause rebaseMultiple to overflow or become extremely large, making all division operations in balanceOf(), totalSupply(), transfer(), etc., revert due to integer division by zero or overflow issues. This effectively halts all token transfers and contract functionality.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The rebase() function allows the owner to multiply rebaseMultiple by any uint256 value. By passing an extremely large multiple, rebaseMultiple becomes huge, causing division operations in balanceOf(), totalSupply(), transfer(), etc., to revert due to overflow or division by zero. This creates a denial of service where no token operations can succeed.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner, set required addresses (rewardsPool and pair), then call rebase() with the maximum possible multiple to make rebaseMultiple extremely large, breaking all token operations.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank
2. Set rewardsPool address to a dummy address
3. Set pair address to a dummy address
4. Calculate maximum multiple: type(uint256).max / current rebaseMultiple
5. Call rebase() with this maximum multiple
6. Verify rebaseMultiple > 1 (oracle condition)
7. Demonstrate that token transfers now revert
attempts.feedback: EVM Revert: call to non-contract address 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005678。请调整参数或调用路径。
